lines.en: I open the door and move out into the hallway.
It’s cold today.
Granted, it’s cold pretty much every day now on account of that whole “Winter” thing-
But it feels even colder than it’s supposed to be, if you know what I’m talking about.
It’s that weird temperature where your clothes seem two sizes tighter than normal and any residual moisture on your hair only slightly-freezes instead of getting completely hard.
It’s a special kind of coldness.
It somehow sneaks in through closed windows and air vents, turning this once-warm sanctuary of sorts into a frozen hellscape.
And there’s someone I know who reminds me a lot of that very specific and particular feeling.
: Hey.
: Yo.
: Why are you just standing with your back to the window like you're trapped in some sort of game CG?
: There’s something I felt the two of us should discuss.
: We haven’t had a substantial conversation since Christmas, and as much as I love that, I can’t go on perpetually ignoring the situation.
: Are you...confessing to me?
: Uhh, what? No. Not even close.
: Worth a shot.
: It’s about our last meeting on the roof. And how the strange level of confidence I had that night bore no fruit whatsoever.
: And what better place to talk about something as serious as that than a hallway full of students, right?
: High school girls are kind of like snow- beautiful, yet fleeting.
: Before you know it, they're gone.
: Look around you. What do you see?
I turn around to find the same strangers as always, passing by and paying little to no attention.
I can’t help but think about the horrible things I would do to some of them if given the opportunity, but for now they’re all just-
: Empty...
: Careful. Your thoughts seem to be spilling out of your head.
: Something like that could prove extremely detrimental to your “career.”
: Do you see what I’m saying now, though?
: That no one is paying any attention and that even if they overheard our conversation they probably wouldn’t think anything of it?
: Oh, wow. You actually do.
: Color me surprised.
: So, what’s going on? Are you trying to blame this[school] thing on our rooftop-meeting?
: That’s just the thing...
: Things have changed before but...never like this.
: An everlasting[school] year filled with the same old faces and the same old seating arrangements-
: That’s all I’ve had for god-knows how long at this point.
: Shouldn’t you be excited that you get to see something new then?
: I believe I’ve made it very apparent that anything new is not ideal for me.
: This also makes me sound like a bit of an idiot- spouting all of those things about how life is a cycle only to have something like this go and happen just shortly after.
: Sounds like a pretty intense inner-struggle you’ve got going on there.
: Yup.
I want to say more to comfort Maya but...
Well, I’m pretty sure that I’m even lower on the list of things that would calm her than having a cavity drilled or having to bury a child.
That second one may be a bit of a stretch, but what I’m essentially saying is that there isn’t anything I can do for her.
Or, at least I don’t think there is.
And I’ll probably always think that since, even now, in her most vulnerable or...confused (?) moments, she’s still miles away from me.
: Like I was saying, I don’t expect you to do anything. Or even care, for that matter.
: I just thought it would only be right to inform you that...
: I might not know what’s coming next.
: But, then again, this could all just be some sort of hiccup.
: A glitch in the matrix, if you will.
: It’s very possible that everything will go back to normal in the middle of the season, the way it’s done so many times before.
: And you’ll have to say goodbye to whoever your next prey may be.
: How come you always need to make me sound like some sort of predator?
: Is that an actual question? Because I’ve got a pretty drawn-out response in the event that it is.
: You can tell me the whole thing on the way home if you want.
: I’m not going home with you. This is exactly why I called you a predator.
: And even if I was, that wouldn't be enough time.
: At least come downstairs with me, then. I’ve already been spending too much time here lately and I want to get out as quickly as I can.
: I suppose I can walk downstairs with you since I also need to do that in order to leave.
: Then it’s a date.
: It most certainly is not.
Maya and I leave the third floor, the one we spend roughly one-third of our lives on, and head toward the lockers.
The snow- Err, the students that crowded the hall just minutes ago have mostly dispersed, leaving several stragglers behind amidst puddles of dirty water in front of the entrance.
Or exit, in some cases.
A door that people move through.
Let’s just call it that.
: You didn’t have to stop at my locker, you know.
: Sorry, I wanted to know where I should be dropping off the love-letter I’ve been writing to you.
: I think it would reach me best if you’d just toss it into the nearest active fireplace.
: Speaking of active fireplaces-
: What can you possibly be segueing into with that?
: Is it really possible for things to go back to normal again after the next reset?
: Oh, something completely unrelated to fireplaces. That’s on-brand.
: I’m not sure...
: The city itself is unfazed by all of the time-skips, it seems.
: It’s the same reason new buildings keep popping up- and how the weather still changes.
: How I imagine it will work if it does go back to normal-
: No, when it goes back to normal- is that the second[school] will go up again and, before long, everyone will filter back in.
: Think of it like buying a new tank and filling it with fish.
: Why do we always need a metaphor? I understood what you meant the first time.
: I like metaphors.
: They’re one of the few things that make everything seem more real.
She’s right about that, at least.
Well, not the metaphor part. The part about how this doesn’t feel real.
Which is a strange thing for me to say given that nothing about this place is real...
But...how can I say this?
A[school] sinking into the ground and everyone having to transfer here? That’s just ridiculous.
Things like that don’t happen.
Entire[school]s don’t fall into the ground.
But I guess when you don’t know what’s beneath you-
: Wait...
: Is that...
: Ooooookay, let’s see here...Building A...West entrance...
: Yup! This is the place!
: Onward to a new path in life!
: Give ‘em Hell, Ushibori!
: Oh god...No way.
: What’s going on? That voice sounds familiar.
Wasn’t Ushibori the last name of the girl transferring into my class? I wonder if-
: Ah! Not even two steps into my new[school] and I’m already seeing friendly faces!
: You’re...going to[school] here now?
: You know it, prin-
: Don’t call me that.
: You know it, Maya!
: And you’re here, too! I knew you two went to this[school] but I had no idea I’d be running into you so soon!
: Hey, hey! You wouldn’t happen to be Mr. Arakawa, would you? Cause that’s Ami’s last name and...by process of elimination...
Uta-chan is going to be in my class.
I’ve never been more thankful for so many people losing their jobs.
: And of course she’s in our class...
: Welcome to the class, Uta. Looks like I’m going to be your new teacher.
: Really!? Like, really-really?!
: Please take good care of me, then!
: I will protect you as if my life depends on it.
: Don’t protect me too much though, okay?
: We don’t want your girlfriend here getting jealous, do we?
: You’re way off, Uta...
: Like, all the way off.
: Oh, please. First you two show up at a maid cafe together...then you ask me to keep it a secret from Ami...
: And now you’re hanging out at the lockers together? Bold move, you two. Bold move.
: Your secret's safe with me, though.
: My dad is like 15 years older than my mom, so I get it. Sometimes you’ve just gotta grab ‘em while they’re still [young]or-
: Okay, I’m leaving now.
: Please don’t follow me.
Maya grabs her things out of her locker and makes for the door without giving Uta or myself a second glance.
I watch her put a green scarf on as she disappears into the snow.
: Just to let you know, I probs can’t call you Master in[school]. I think that would get both of us in lots of trouble.
: You can call me whatever you want.
: Okay, Maya’s boyfriend!
: Uhh, maybe not anything, actually.
: I know how it looks but the two of us really aren’t like that.
: Really? Well that’s good, at least.
: Cause...this might sound kinda weird, but I’m pretty sure Ami has the hots for you.
: Can you imagine the drama that would spark up if you were dating her best friend?
: But it is what it is! I’m just super excited to have somebody I know as my teacher!
: I’ll be a good girl in class, okay? You won’t even know I’m there.
: Oh and if you could like, never call on me for any science question...or math question...
: Or Japanese question...or English question...
Is there anything I can call on her for?
Wait, I don’t ever call on anyone for anything.
: Let me stop you right there and inform you that your life is about to get immensely easier.
: Easier? What do you mean?
: You’re not gonna try and propose one of those “I scratch your back, you scratch mine” things, are you? Cause I’m supposed to let my parents know whenever I start doing that kind of stuff.
: Also you’re like a billion times my size. It's kind of intimidating, not gonna lie.
: As thrilled as I am to hear that those are the only two barriers to entry-
: Three counting your girlfriend.
: Three counting the girlfriend who is not my girlfriend-
: Or so he says.
: What I mean is that I’ll basically just let you do whatever you want in class.
: Aww, that’s so sweet of you...But you really don’t have to give me special treatment just because I’m a super cute maid by night.
: I promise I’ll work just as hard for you in the cafe even if you work me to the bone in[school].
: It’s not special treatment. I do the same thing for everyone.
: And you still get to keep your job?!
: Surprisingly, yes.
: AHHHHH THIS SCHOOL IS ALREADY SO MUCH FRIGGIN’ BETTER!
: Hey! Umm, I don’t know if it was just some lame rumor going around but...do I really get to stay in a dorm?
: Cause if that’s true, I’m gonna flip out.
: Did they really not tell you anything about how it works here?
: I’m on my way to talk to the principal about all that stuff now, but you can spoil the surprise for me if you want.
: In fact, please spoil me. I need to know.
: Unless they changed something, yes, you’ll get to stay in a dorm.
: THIS IS SO HECKIN’ AWESOME OH MY GOD!
: Sensei!...which I guess is my new name for you when I’m not in uniform-
: I’m gonna go to my meeting thingy now. But I’ll see you in class tomorrow, right?! Right?!
: You certainly will.
: Have fun at your “meeting thingy.”
: I’LL HAVE SO MUCH FUN, YOU WON’T EVEN UNDERSTAND IT!
Uta sprints down the hallway (And the wrong one, might I add) and I already don’t understand how much fun she’s having.
The last thing my class needs is another loud and obnoxious girl, but...
I will gladly make an exception for Uta.
In fact, I’d probably kill for her if she asked me to.
That’s an incredibly dangerous thing to admit, but...
I’m pretty sure it might actually be true.
I guess the Uta I know isn’t the same one I’ll be seeing every day from now on, but still-
She seems lively and friendly enough that the two of us will get along great once we get to spend some time together...
Uta’s affection has increased to [uta_love]!
